discovery: Infinite-dimensional conformal symmetry and the exact solution of two-dimensional critical phenomena (conformal field theory)

nominees.name: Alexander A. Belavin
nominees.affiliation: L.D. Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics, Russia

subfield: Statistical physics and quantum field theory
motivation: In 1984 Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov showed that at a two-dimensional critical point scale invariance becomes an infinite-dimensional conformal symmetry, governed by the Virasoro algebra. From this simple principle they derived exactly the critical exponents and correlation functions of whole families of statistical systems (the minimal models, including the Ising and Potts universality classes) without solving any microscopic Hamiltonian. The idea revealed a hidden order underlying critical fluctuations and became a universal language: it describes surface and polymer critical behaviour, quantum Hall edges, quantum spin chains, entanglement entropy, string theory and holography, and it inspired the modern conformal bootstrap, which now gives the most precise values for the three-dimensional Ising exponents. Zamolodchikov's c-theorem and integrable perturbations extended it to the renormalisation-group flow itself. Few theoretical discoveries have shaped how physicists understand collective behaviour so deeply and across so many fields.
